Research indicates that small language models (SLMs) face challenges in providing reliable confidence signals, particularly through token-level entropy, which often yields near-zero mean entropy across various datasets. By employing semantic entropy, improvements in accuracy can be achieved by routing uncertain queries to larger expert models, demonstrating a more effective allocation of computational resources.

 - Small language models struggle with token-level confidence signals due to low entropy values.
 - Semantic entropy can significantly enhance accuracy by routing uncertain queries to larger models.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20824

Research on small language models (SLMs) reveals that token-level entropy signals are largely ineffective, with 91% of evaluations showing near-zero token entropy regardless of correctness. In contrast, semantic entropy, derived from generating and clustering answers, provides a useful confidence signal and can significantly enhance accuracy by selectively routing queries to larger expert models, achieving improvements of up to +50 percentage points.

 - Token-level entropy is ineffective in small language models, showing near-zero values in most cases.
 - Semantic entropy can improve the performance of language models by directing uncertain queries to larger models.

Research indicates that the decision problem for the Closest Vector Problem (CVP) within the framework of principal cyclotomic ideals has been proven NP-complete.  - Exact decision-CVP on principal cyclotomic ideals is NP-complete.

Such developments imply that a polynomial-time solution to this problem could collapse established complexity hierarchies.

 - Exact decision-CVP for principal cyclotomic ideals is NP-complete.

Category: Cybersecurity
Importance: 8
Vision Transformers (ViTs) are being used in split-inference systems where intermediate token representations are sent to the cloud, but these systems are susceptible to feature inversion attacks that can reconstruct input images. New techniques such as token reduction and shuffling provide some privacy benefits, yet significant risks of information leakage remain. Researchers developed a new attack method that demonstrates how even with these defenses, position information within the tokens can be exploited to recover original inputs.

 - Feature inversion attacks can reconstruct input images from intermediate representations used in ViT split-inference systems.
 - Token reduction and shuffling offer limited privacy protections, and a new attack methodology reveals persistent vulnerabilities.
 - A proposed edge-side defense reduces the risk of attacks while maintaining the accuracy of the cloud-side model.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01232

A finite connected simple cubic graph has been constructed that challenges the Bilu–Linial signing conjecture, proving it false for general regular graphs. The specific graph demonstrates that all edge signings yield an eigenvalue outside a defined range. While this finding is significant, the conjecture related to Ramanujan base graphs is still unresolved.

 - A new counterexample to the Bilu–Linial signing conjecture has been presented.
 - The graph constructed is not Ramanujan, leaving open questions about similar conjectures.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15591
